name: YugabyteDB
tagline: Apache-licensed distributed SQL that reuses the PostgreSQL query layer on a Raft-replicated storage engine.
description: YugabyteDB is a distributed database that grafts the actual PostgreSQL query layer (YSQL) onto DocDB, a sharded, Raft-replicated storage engine derived from RocksDB. Because it reuses Postgres code rather than reimplementing it, compatibility with triggers, stored procedures, extensions like pgvector and most ORMs is unusually high for a distributed system. A second API, YCQL, speaks the Cassandra query language for wide-column workloads. It is a sensible pick when you want Postgres semantics plus horizontal write scaling and multi-region resilience under a permissive license, and you can accept somewhat higher per-query latency than single-node Postgres.

pricing.notes: Database is free and open source; YugabyteDB Aeon (managed) has a free Sandbox cluster; YugabyteDB Anywhere (self-managed control plane) is commercial.

scale.notes: Hash and range sharding into tablets with automatic rebalancing; supports synchronous multi-region clusters, xCluster async replication and geo-partitioning.

strengths: Reuses PostgreSQL's own query layer, so triggers, stored procedures and many extensions work
Fully Apache 2.0 database core, including enterprise-grade features like encryption and xCluster
Synchronous multi-region writes or async xCluster replication, chosen per deployment
Cassandra-compatible YCQL API alongside SQL in the same cluster
Online tablet splitting and rebalancing as nodes are added
weaknesses: Higher latency per statement than single-node Postgres, especially for chatty ORMs
Postgres version lags upstream (YSQL tracks an older major release)
Cross-shard joins and foreign keys can be slow without careful colocation
Operational footprint (masters, tservers, tuning flags) is heavier than plain Postgres
useCases: Scaling a Postgres application beyond one primary
Multi-region customer and order data with zone/region resilience
Retail and financial OLTP needing horizontal write capacity
IoT and telemetry metadata with TTL on YCQL tables
Migrating off Cassandra while gaining SQL
notIdealFor: Small single-region apps where Postgres is simpler
